# AGENTS.md

Pure-Bun Codex gateway: ChatCompletions <-> Responses for the Codex desktop/CLI
app, zero npm dependencies. Declared models route to chat (OpenAI-compatible)
*or* Responses providers; undeclared models pass through to the signed-in
ChatGPT backend. Distributed as a compiled binary (`bun run build` ->
`codextras`); run it wherever you install it and state/, logs/,
codextras.json resolve next to it.

## Commands

    codextras start|stop|status       daemonize via pidfile
    codextras catalog                 declared-models catalog
    codextras catalog-merged          capture native catalog + write state/merged-models.json
    codextras dry-run [alias]         render future config.toml without writing
    codextras apply [alias]           backup + switch ~/.codex/config.toml to codextras
    codextras restore                 restore the pre-codextras config.toml
    bun run build                     compile the binary (src/cli.mjs)
    bun test                          unit tests (stop the gateway first: port conflict)
    ./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh    live checks (needs gateway running + real upstream key)

## Architecture

    src/server.mjs          Bun.serve: /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/models, WS refused with 426
    src/adapter.mjs         chat + Responses builders (thinking envelope, efforts, include, store, stream_options)
    src/convert/request.mjs Responses items -> chat messages (reasoning, tools, images, compaction) + flattenToolsForResponses
    src/convert/tools.mjs   custom/freeform tool bridge (exec etc.)
    src/convert/stream.mjs  chat SSE -> Responses SSE lifecycle (responses upstream is proxied verbatim)
    src/convert/json.mjs    non-streaming chat -> Responses
    src/catalog.mjs         catalog entry generation + native merge + visibility overrides (supports_reasoning_summaries toggleable)
    src/codex-config.mjs    config.toml managed-block rendering
    src/compaction.mjs      compaction v1/v2 with kcr1: summary envelope (chat or responses per provider)

## Onboarding: configure a model

Edit `codextras.json`. Providers are OpenAI-compatible chat **or Responses**
endpoints; `provider.type` (or `wireApi`/`api`) selects the wire format.
`type: "openai-chat"` (default) → `/chat/completions` with Chat↔Responses
bridging (needed for DeepSeek); `type: "openai-responses"` →
`/responses` with verbatim Responses passthrough (needed for Muse Spark,
preserves `reasoning.encrypted_content` + true multimodal). All three
dimensions are toggleable per-model: vision via `inputModalities` +
`imagePassthrough`, wire format via `provider.type` *or* `model.wireApi`/`model.api`,
and reasoning via `reasoningInjection`/`disableThoughtHack` +
`reasoningSummary`/`supportsReasoningSummaries`. Quirks carry per-provider
differences as data (thinking envelope, effort aliases, stream_options,
`include`). Relative `apiKeyFile` paths resolve against the repo root.

Example (opencode-go provider + DeepSeek V4 Flash):

```json
{
  "gateway": { "port": 4200, "pathPrefix": "/_codextras" },
  "providers": [
    {
      "id": "opencode-go",
      "type": "openai-chat",
      "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1",
      "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY", "OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY"],
      "apiKeyFile": "./state/opencode-go-api-key.secret",
      "quirks": {
        "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
        "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" },
        "streamOptions": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "models": [
    {
      "alias": "deepseek-flash",
      "displayName": "V4 Flash",
      "provider": "opencode-go",
      "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash",
      "contextWindow": 1048576,
      "autoCompact": 900000,
      "efforts": ["low", "high", "max"],
      "defaultEffort": "high",
      "inputModalities": ["text", "image"],
      "imagePassthrough": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Then `codextras apply <alias>` and restart the Codex app (it caches the
catalog). `catalogOverrides` can force native-model visibility (e.g.
`{"gpt-5.2": {"visibility": "hide"}}`).

Dual-provider example (DeepSeek on chat + Muse Spark on Responses, same key):

```json
{
  "providers": [
    { "id": "opencode-go-chat", "type": "openai-chat", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "thinking": { "type": "enabled" }, "efforts": { "low": "low", "high": "high", "max": "max" } } },
    { "id": "opencode-go-responses", "type": "openai-responses", "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1", "apiKeyEnv": ["OPENCODE_API_KEY"], "quirks": { "efforts": { "minimal": "minimal", "low": "low", "medium": "medium", "high": "high", "xhigh": "xhigh" }, "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], "reasoningSummary": "auto", "store": false } }
  ],
  "models": [
    { "alias": "deepseek-flash", "provider": "opencode-go-chat", "upstreamModel": "deepseek-v4-flash", "efforts": ["low","high","max"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": false },
    { "alias": "muse-spark", "provider": "opencode-go-responses", "upstreamModel": "muse-spark-1.2", "efforts": ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"], "defaultEffort": "high", "inputModalities": ["text","image"], "imagePassthrough": true, "supportsReasoningSummaries": true, "reasoningSummary": "auto" }
  ]
}
```
Alternative single-provider toggle: set `"api": "responses"` (or `wireApi`/`targetApi`) per `models[]` entry to override the provider’s wire format — same `type` field works per-model. Vision (`imagePassthrough`), wire format, and `<thought>` hack are all toggleable.

## Hard-won constraints

- The managed block in config.toml must stay at the TOP of the file: root keys
  (`openai_base_url`, `model_catalog_json`) land inside whatever table precedes
  them otherwise, and Codex silently ignores them.
- Reasoning is preserved twice for **chat** providers: `reasoning_content` on
  assistant messages (the DeepSeek API contract when tools are present) AND a
  visible `<thought>` block (the model's only real memory). Never use
  `<think>`: the upstream's reasoning parser strips that exact tag from
  assistant content. **Responses** providers (Muse Spark) do not use this
  hack — they replay `reasoning.encrypted_content` via `include` + `store:false`
  and should disable it with `reasoningInjection:"none"` / `disableThoughtHack`.
  Muse’s `summary` is empty today (encrypted only).
- Custom tools (exec) are advertised as functions with a single required
  `content` string property and returned as `custom_tool_call` items (see
  convert/tools.mjs). This mirrors the proven LiteLLM bridge; the app's tool
  router rejects plain `function_call` items for freeform tools.
- Catalog entries require `experimental_supported_tools` and should set
  `prefer_websockets: false`; Codex falls back to its built-in catalog if the
  file fails to parse.
- WebSocket upgrades get `426` on purpose: Codex falls back to HTTP streaming
  immediately. Do not add a WS endpoint.
- `state/` and `logs/` hold secrets (gateway token, provider API key, catalog
  JSONs). Never commit them.

## Verification loop

1. `codextras stop && bun test && codextras start`
2. `./smoke/verify-after-switch.sh` (health, config.toml root keys, catalog,
   real upstream turn, compaction, WS 426)
3. `codextras apply <alias>`, then the Codex app must be fully quit and
   reopened to reload the catalog.

## Conventions

Bun-only, no npm dependencies, no build step. Match the existing style (ESM,
plain functions, minimal abstraction). Add unit tests for conversion logic in
test/gateway.test.mjs; live behaviors belong in the smoke script.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

333: // Plain `codex debug models` returns the effective catalog, which includes
334: // our own merged file (Codex loads it via model_catalog_json). The fake
335: // binary below reproduces that: --bundled is pristine, plain is polluted
336: // with a stale declared model. Capture must prefer --bundled so removed
337: // models never resurrect in the native cache.
338: function writeFakeCodexBin(dir, { failBundled = false } = {}) {
339:   const fakeBin = path.join(dir, "codex");
340:   writeFileSync(
341:     fakeBin,
342:     `#!/usr/bin/env bun
343: const args = process.argv.slice(2);
344: if (${failBundled ? "true" : "false"} && args.includes("--bundled")) process.exit(1);
345: const pristine = { models: [{ slug: "gpt-5.6-sol", display_name: "GPT-5.6 Sol", visibility: "list", priority: 1, supported_in_api: true }] };
346: const polluted = { models: [...pristine.models, { slug: "deepseek-flash", display_name: "V4 Flash", visibility: "list", priority: 1, supported_in_api: true }] };
347: console.log(JSON.stringify(args.includes("--bundled") ? pristine : polluted));
348: `,
349:   );
350:   chmodSync(fakeBin, 0o755);
351:   return fakeBin;
352: }

1: // Native OpenAI passthrough: requests for models that are not declared in
2: // codextras.json are forwarded to the signed-in ChatGPT backend, exactly like
3: // codex-router does, so OpenAI models keep working alongside routed models.
4: 
5: const FORWARD_HEADERS = new Set([
6:   "authorization",
7:   "chatgpt-account-id",
8:   "openai-beta",
9:   "originator",
10:   "session_id",
11:   "session-id",
12:   "thread-id",
13:   "x-client-request-id",
14:   "x-codex-beta-features",
15:   "x-codex-installation-id",
16:   "x-codex-parent-thread-id",
17:   "x-codex-turn-metadata",
18:   "x-codex-turn-state",
19:   "x-codex-window-id",
20:   "x-oai-attestation",
21:   "x-openai-subagent",
22:   "x-responsesapi-include-timing-metrics",
23: ]);
24: 
25: export function nativeBase() {
26:   return String(
27:     process.env.CODEXTRAS_NATIVE_BASE_URL ||
28:       "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex",
29:   ).replace(/\/+$/, "");
30: }
31: 
32: export function nativeTarget(apiPath, search) {
33:   const withoutV1 = apiPath.replace(/^\/v1(?=\/|$)/, "");
34:   return nativeBase() + withoutV1 + (search || "");
35: }
36: 
37: export function forwardedHeaders(request) {
38:   const headers = {
39:     "Content-Type": "application/json",
40:     "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
41:   };
42:   for (const name of FORWARD_HEADERS) {
43:     const value = request.headers.get(name);
44:     if (value !== undefined && value !== null && value !== "") {
45:       headers[name] = value;
46:     }
47:   }
48:   return headers;
49: }
50: 
51: export async function forwardNative(request, apiPath, rawBody) {

11:   const outputTokens = tokenCount(value.output_tokens ?? value.completion_tokens);

else if (output.every((p) => p && typeof p.text === "string")) output = output.map((p) => p.text).join("\n");

// Keep at least the text if message was only an image tag that got stripped but original had <image ...> text
const rawText = Array.isArray(item.content) ? item.content.map((p) => (p && typeof p.text === "string" ? p.text : "")).join("").trim() : "";
out.push({ type: "message", role, content: [{ type: t, text: rawText }] });
if (text) out.push({ type: "message", role: "user", content: [{ type: "input_text", text }] });
const text = summary ? SUMMARY_PREFIX + "\n\n" + summary : "Earlier conversation history was compacted in an unreadable format.";
out.push({ type: "message", role: "user", content: [{ type: "input_text", text }] });

1: // Shared bridge for "custom" (freeform) tools such as exec. Chat-completions
2: // providers can only express function tools, so custom tools are advertised as
3: // functions with a single `content` string property; when the model calls one,
4: // the raw payload is recovered from that property and delivered to the host as
5: // a `custom_tool_call` item, which is the shape the app's tool router expects
6: // for freeform tools. Mirrors the proven LiteLLM bridge so the streaming and
7: // non-streaming response paths share one code path.
8: 
9: export function extractCustomToolNames(tools) {
10:   const names = new Set();
11:   if (!Array.isArray(tools)) return names;
12:   for (const tool of tools) {
13:     if (
14:       tool &&
15:       typeof tool === "object" &&
16:       tool.type === "custom" &&
17:       typeof tool.name === "string"
18:     ) {
19:       names.add(tool.name);
20:     }
21:   }
22:   return names;
23: }
24: 
25: const MAX_ARGUMENTS_LEN = 1_000_000;
26: 
27: export function unwrapCustomToolArguments(argumentsString) {
28:   if (!argumentsString) return "";
29:   if (argumentsString.length > MAX_ARGUMENTS_LEN) return argumentsString;
30:   try {
31:     const parsed = JSON.parse(argumentsString);
32:     if (parsed && typeof parsed === "object" && typeof parsed.content === "string") {
33:       return parsed.content;
34:     }
35:   } catch {
36:     // Not JSON; the raw arguments string is the input.
37:   }
38:   return argumentsString;
39: }
40: 
41: function normalizeToolArguments(args) {
42:   if (args === undefined || args === null) return "{}";
43:   if (typeof args === "string") {
44:     const trimmed = args.trim();
45:     if (!trimmed) return "{}";
46:     try {
47:       JSON.parse(trimmed);
48:       return trimmed;
49:     } catch {
50:       return "{}";
51:     }
52:   }
53:   if (typeof args === "object") {
54:     try {
55:       const s = JSON.stringify(args);
56:       if (s) {
57:         JSON.parse(s);
58:         return s;
59:       }
60:     } catch {}
61:     return "{}";
62:   }
63:   return "{}";
64: }

66: export function toolCallItem({ callId, name, args, status, customNames }) {
67:   const custom = customNames instanceof Set && customNames.has(name);
68:   const item = {
69:     id: callId,
70:     type: custom ? "custom_tool_call" : "function_call",
71:     status,
72:     call_id: callId,
73:     name,
74:   };
75:   if (custom) {
76:     item.input = status === "completed" ? unwrapCustomToolArguments(args) : "";
77:   } else {
78:     item.arguments = normalizeToolArguments(args);
79:   }

1: // Content-encoding helpers: the desktop client and some upstreams send
2: // zstd/gzip/deflate/br bodies. Bun's fetch auto-decompresses when
3: // Content-Encoding is present, but Bun.serve does NOT decompress inbound
4: // bodies, and some upstreams send raw compressed frames without any
5: // Content-Encoding header. All gateway JSON/SSE reads go through here so
6: // both labeled and magic-sniffed frames decode correctly.
7: 
8: import {
9:   brotliDecompressSync,
10:   gunzipSync,
11:   inflateRawSync,
12:   inflateSync,
13: } from "node:zlib";
14: 
15: function nodeZstdDecompressSync(input) {
16:   // node:zlib ships zstd on recent runtimes; prefer it, fall back to Bun.
17:   try {
18:     const zlib = require("node:zlib");
19:     if (zlib && typeof zlib.zstdDecompressSync === "function") {
20:       return zlib.zstdDecompressSync(input);
21:     }
22:   } catch {}
23:   return Bun.zstdDecompressSync(input);
24: }
25: 
26: export function parseContentEncoding(header) {
27:   if (!header || typeof header !== "string") return [];
28:   return header
29:     .split(",")
30:     .map((s) => s.trim().toLowerCase())
31:     .filter(Boolean)
32:     .filter((v) => v !== "identity");
33: }
34: 
35: export function sniffEncoding(buf) {
36:   if (!buf || buf.length < 2) return null;
37:   if (
38:     buf.length >= 4 &&
39:     buf[0] === 0x28 &&
40:     buf[1] === 0xb5 &&
41:     buf[2] === 0x2f &&
42:     buf[3] === 0xfd
43:   ) {
44:     return "zstd";
45:   }
46:   if (buf[0] === 0x1f && buf[1] === 0x8b) return "gzip";
47:   // zlib-wrapped deflate: 0x78 01 / 0x78 9c / 0x78 da are the common headers.
48:   if (buf[0] === 0x78 && (buf[1] === 0x01 || buf[1] === 0x9c || buf[1] === 0xda)) {
49:     return "deflate";
50:   }
51:   return null;
52: }
53: 
54: function decompressOne(buf, encoding) {
55:   const input = Buffer.isBuffer(buf) ? buf : Buffer.from(buf);
56:   switch (encoding) {
57:     case "zstd":
58:     case "x-zstd":
59:     case "zstandard":
60:       return Buffer.from(nodeZstdDecompressSync(input));
61:     case "gzip":
62:     case "x-gzip":
63:       return Buffer.from(gunzipSync(input));
64:     case "deflate":
65:       try {
66:         return Buffer.from(inflateSync(input));
67:       } catch {
68:         return Buffer.from(inflateRawSync(input));
69:       }
70:     case "br":
71:     case "brotli":
72:       return Buffer.from(brotliDecompressSync(input));
73:     default:
74:       throw new Error("unsupported content-encoding: " + encoding);
75:   }
76: }
77: 
78: // Decompress `bytes` according to the Content-Encoding header (applied in
79: // reverse, per RFC) plus magic-byte sniffing for raw frames that arrive
80: // without a header. Already-plain bodies (e.g. fetch already decompressed
81: // but left the header in place) pass through untouched: decompressing plain
82: // JSON throws, and we keep the original bytes.
83: export function decompressBuffer(bytes, contentEncodingHeader) {
84:   let buf = Buffer.isBuffer(bytes) ? bytes : Buffer.from(bytes || []);
85:   if (!buf.length) return buf;
86:   const encodings = parseContentEncoding(contentEncodingHeader);
87:   for (let i = encodings.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
88:     const enc = encodings[i];
89:     try {
90:       buf = decompressOne(buf, enc);
91:     } catch {
92:       // Keep bytes as-is; sniffing below may still apply.
93:     }
94:   }
95:   for (let iter = 0; iter < 3; iter += 1) {
96:     const sniffed = sniffEncoding(buf);
97:     if (!sniffed) break;
98:     try {
99:       buf = decompressOne(buf, sniffed);
100:     } catch {
101:       break;
102:     }
103:   }
104:   return buf;
105: }
106: 
107: export function decodeBodyToString(bytes, contentEncodingHeader) {
108:   return decompressBuffer(bytes, contentEncodingHeader).toString("utf8");
109: }
110: 
111: export function parseJsonBody(bytes, contentEncodingHeader) {
112:   return JSON.parse(decodeBodyToString(bytes, contentEncodingHeader));
113: }
114: 
115: // Robust upstream JSON read: fetch usually decompresses labeled bodies, but
116: // raw zstd/gzip frames without Content-Encoding arrive still compressed.
117: // Sniff the magic bytes so both cases parse. Returns `fallback` on failure
118: // to preserve the previous `res.json().catch(() => ({}))` contract.
119: export async function readUpstreamJson(res, fallback) {
120:   const fb = fallback !== undefined ? fallback : {};
121:   try {
122:     const raw = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());
123:     const enc = res && res.headers ? res.headers.get("content-encoding") : null;
124:     const buf = decompressBuffer(raw, enc);
125:     const text = buf.toString("utf8").trim();
126:     if (!text) return fb;
127:     return JSON.parse(text);
128:   } catch {
129:     return fb;
130:   }
131: }
132: 
133: // Same idea for upstream error bodies: prefer a decompressed message.
134: export async function readUpstreamText(res) {
135:   try {
136:     const raw = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());
137:     // arrayBuffer() consumes the body; callers must not read it again.
138:     const enc = res && res.headers ? res.headers.get("content-encoding") : null;
139:     return decompressBuffer(raw, enc).toString("utf8");
140:   } catch {
141:     return "";
142:   }
143: }
144: 
145: // Collect an upstream streaming body (SSE) into decompressed bytes. Plain
146: // streams pass through; raw compressed frames without a header are inflated
147: // first. Callers split the returned text into SSE blocks as usual.
148: export async function readUpstreamStreamBytes(res) {
149:   const raw = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());
150:   const enc = res && res.headers ? res.headers.get("content-encoding") : null;
151:   return decompressBuffer(raw, enc);
152: }

Fixed zstd (and gzip/deflate/br) handling — the gateway was blowing up because `Bun.serve` never inflates inbound bodies and raw upstream frames arrive without `Content-Encoding`.

**Root cause:**
- Desktop client sends `Content-Encoding: zstd` bodies → `JSON.parse(rawBytes)` failed → `400 Request body must be a JSON object` (surfaced as “response is not a JSON object”).
- Some upstreams send raw zstd/gzip frames with `Content-Type: application/json` but no `Content-Encoding` → `fetch` doesn’t inflate → `res.json()` fell back to `{}` → empty `output: []`, truncated SSE.

**Fix (`src/` only, `bun test` 38/38 green):**
- `src/encoding.mjs` (new): `decompressBuffer` handles `zstd/gzip/deflate/br` via header (reverse order) + magic sniff (`28 B5 2F FD` for zstd, `1F 8B` for gzip, `78 …` for deflate). Already-plain bodies pass through (failed inflate keeps original, avoiding double-decode when `fetch` already inflated but left the header). Helpers `readUpstreamJson`/`readUpstreamText`/`upstreamByteChunks` (streaming preserves incremental delivery for plain SSE, buffers+inflates only when sniffed/binary).
- `src/server.mjs`: inbound `arrayBuffer` → `decompressBuffer(..., content-encoding)` before `JSON.parse`, forwards inflated bytes to native; upstream `res.text()/res.json()` → `readUpstreamText/Json`; `sseEvents`/`streamResponsesTurn` iterate `upstreamByteChunks`.
- `src/compaction.mjs`: `res.json()` → `readUpstreamJson`.
- `src/native.mjs`: preserves upstream `content-encoding` on proxied responses.

Verified: inbound `zstd/gzip/br/deflate` + raw sniff, upstream raw/with-header JSON+SSE for both chat and Responses wires, native passthrough, compaction, and compressed error bodies all decode correctly.
